question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 04 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The increase in p95 latency is due to a reduction in the database pool size, leading to connection exhaustion.
why_chain: The config_change (E5) reduced the auth db.pool_size from 50 to 5.
This reduction in pool size caused more connections to be exhausted, leading to the warning logs (E7, E8, E9).
The exhausted connections resulted in longer latency, as the system had to wait for a free connection.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a configuration change in another service.
ruled_out.reason: The config_change (E5) is the only change in configuration that is relevant to the auth service.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a network issue.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of network issues (e.g., network latency, packet loss, etc.).

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a dependency issue with an external service.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of any external service issues or changes.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a sudden increase in request volume, which overwhelmed the system.
ruled_out.reason: It rests on a change that is too early, or in a different service/region, to explain a sudden change here.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for service auth rose from 91 ms to 253 ms (+179%), with a change point at 2026-03-04T12:00:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service auth: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for service auth stayed about the same (1097 per 5 min before, 1344 per 5 min after, +23%).
At the same time, error rate for service auth rose (0.35% before, 0.54% after, +55%).
Changed auth db.pool_size from 50 to 5 (all regions) (auth; 3 min before the change; record R019; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
p95 latency above SLO on auth (auth; 15 min after the change; record R021; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
auth: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (auth, ap-south; 13 min after the change; record R020; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
auth: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (auth, eu-west; 19 min after the change; record R022; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
auth: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (auth, us-east; 24 min after the change; record R023; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (3 min before the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Increase the db.pool_size back to 50 to resolve the connection exhaustion issue.
